O.content: The title visibly reads “Incidence of Condition A in US States.”

A vertical color bar runs from pale yellow at its top to dark burgundy at its bottom; “High” is printed beside the top, “Low” beside the bottom, and printed ticks include 100 at the top and 0 at the bottom.
The inscription “WV” is placed inside a pale-yellow state polygon.
The inscription “UT” is placed inside a dark-burgundy state polygon.
A gray state polygon is visible in the position where the Alabama option would refer, but that polygon has no visible “AL” inscription and gray is not shown on the legend.

B.text: For this choropleth, a state's fill color encodes incidence according to the vertical legend: the pale-yellow end adjacent to the printed 100 and “High” is higher than the dark-burgundy end adjacent to the printed 0 and “Low.” If the gray Alabama-area polygon denotes unmapped/no incidence value rather than a value on that scale, it is not eligible to exceed a mapped state; among the offered eligible state records, route the highest-incidence one.
B.conditions: Applies only if the legend governs the state fills and gray is an unmapped/missing category. The chart does not visibly print an Alabama label or define gray.
